Do auxiliary crystal views beat the structure graph alone?

Every cell trains one crystal-property regressor for 150 epochs and compares a structure-only graph (S) against the same model given simulated Cu Kα powder XRD (X), a space-group symmetry embedding (G), or both. Within a task, backbone and seed, the split, normalizer, optimizer and schedule are identical — only the auxiliary input changes.

Does each view help?

Gain is MAE(S) − MAE(view), averaged over seeds and paired sample by sample; the interval is a reduced-formula cluster bootstrap (10,000 replicates, seed 42). Seed agreement is only meaningful once all three seeds of a pair have finished.

Error by view

MAE and RMSE are in the task's own target unit and are the mean over seeds of the per-seed test metrics; the spread is the standard deviation across seeds. nMAE divides MAE by the test-target standard deviation, which is the only column comparable between tasks. The best MAE in each row group is highlighted.

Backbone qualification

A pair enters the grid only if its structure-only baseline trains to completion, keeps finite metrics and non-degenerate prediction variance, and beats a constant train-mean predictor. Flagged adds a stability concern (validation spike ratio above 10, or a final/best validation ratio above 1.5) and the flag travels with every number it produces.

Task suite

Matbench and the Materials Project tasks share MP provenance, and the four JARVIS tasks share one structure collection, so these are not independent dataset replicates.

Held runs

A diverged or collapsed model is a scientific outcome, not a job to retry: those runs are preserved and never requeued. Only infrastructure faults are rerun, with the identical configuration.
